title: Tenant-aware coalescer and adaptive compaction for KV cache
content:
Summary:
This note proposes a tenant-aware coalescing layer and an adaptive compaction policy for the KV cache aimed at reducing fragmentation and improving tail-latency predictability in multi-tenant serving clusters. The core idea is to move away from fixed-size slab buckets toward a lightweight per-tenant allocation stripe with opportunistic coalescing of small, cold fragments and throttled, size-aware compaction windows. The design trades off a small amount of CPU for measurable reductions in memory waste and read-amplification during eviction/rehydration cycles.

Goals and constraints:
- Primary goal: lower usable-memory fragmentation across mixed tenant workloads (many small prefixes + a few large sessions) while preserving low tail latency for hot prefixes.
- Secondary goals: preserve tenant isolation (soft quotas), avoid global stop-the-world compaction pauses, and keep runtime changes low-risk for rollouts.
- Constraints: must be implementable without kernel changes, work within existing allocator interfaces, and be compatible with current prefix/KV lookup paths and KV cache persistence semantics.

Key observations motivating this design:
1) Fragmentation is workload-driven: many short-lived prefix allocations (e.g., 4–32B keys with small value payloads) leave behind holes that are expensive to reclaim with large global compactions.
2) Tenant locality: requests overwhelmingly belong to a small subset of tenants at any given time; co-locating a tenant’s allocations improves the chance of contiguous free space when the tenant shrinks.
3) Compaction costs are proportional to moved bytes and created write-amplification; we should prefer compaction windows with high expected reclaimable space.

Design overview (high level):
- Per-tenant stripes: each tenant gets a small set of allocation stripes (logical arenas) mapped to physical pages. Stripes favor same-size runs for short-lived allocations and are adjustable at runtime.
- Slabless variable-size allocator within stripes: rather than rigid slab classes we use a best-fit-ish free-list within the stripe with a lightweight size-binning for small buckets (4B..1KB). This reduces internal fragmentation for the common small-value case.
- Tenant-aware coalescer: background task that watches per-tenant fragmentation metrics and opportunistically coalesces adjacent free runs into larger contiguous spans when thresholded. Coalescing is localized to a tenant’s stripes to preserve isolation and reduce locking.
- Adaptive compaction windows: instead of global compaction, schedule tenant-specific compaction worklets when (a) tenant free-ratio crosses X, (b) estimated reclaimable bytes exceed a threshold T, and (c) QoS headroom exists on the node. The compaction migrates live KV entries into new contiguous spans and frees old ranges.
- Size-aware eviction policy: eviction prioritizes items not solely by LRU. We use a metric we call SGA (size-adjusted age): score = age_seconds / log(1 + size_bytes). Eviction selects items with high score but also factors in tenant soft quotas.

Memory layout and allocation details:
- Physical pages are divided into stripe-aligned segments (default segment = 2MB). Each tenant stripe is assigned 1..N segments based on current working set and quota. Within a segment we store a simple header + packed items. Allocation metadata is maintained in a compact slotmap per segment (bitmap + small-size metadata for occupied slots).
- Small-value path: values <= 1KB are packed with prefix-length and a 2-byte length field. The allocator uses micro-bins (4B, 8B, 16B, 32B, 64B, 128B, 256B, 512B, 1KB) to speed allocation. Deallocation marks the slot free in the bitmap and appends the range to a per-stripe free-run list.
- Large-value path: values > 1KB are allocated as contiguous multi-page runs and tracked in the same slotmap but with an explicit run-length field. Large runs are placed at end-of-segment preferentially to minimize split fragments.

Fragmentation and coalescing heuristics:
- Fragmentation metric F_tenant = 1 - (largest_contiguous_free_span / total_free_bytes). This yields 0 for perfect contiguity and approaches 1 for highly fragmented tenants.
- Coalescer trigger: if F_tenant > 0.35 AND reclaimable_bytes > 8MB, schedule coalescer work for that tenant. The coalescer scans stripe slotmaps and attempts to merge adjacent runs into larger spans.
- Opportunistic in-band coalescing: individual allocations that would create small leftover holes (<= 256B) will instead trigger an in-band compaction of the small neighborhood if the allocation latency budget allows (e.g., request isn't latency-sensitive or request path has extra slack).

Adaptive compaction policy details:
- Cost model: compaction cost C = bytes_moved * move_cost_factor + CPU_ms. Benefit B = bytes_reclaimed * expected_cost_per_byte_saved (including future eviction/rehydration savings). We schedule compaction when B > C * safety_multiplier. Move_cost_factor and expected_cost_per_byte_saved are calibrated from production telemetry.
- Throttling: compaction tasks use a token-bucket that charges per-moved-byte; the token refill rate is adjustable per-node and per-tier (hosted vs dedicated). This prevents compaction from starving inference threads.
- Migration ordering: compact coldest-first within the tenant to reduce reaccess churn. Avoid moving very hot prefixes unless necessary for fragmentation reduction.

Eviction and tenant quotas integration:
- Soft quotas: each tenant has an adjustable soft quota shared with the scheduler layer. When a tenant exceeds soft_quota * 1.0, eviction policy favors items from that tenant. When a tenant exceeds hard_quota, the runtime will reject non-critical writes or offload to disk (configurable).
- Eviction selection: combine SGA score with tenant-penalty term to ensure noisy neighbors can’t evict a tenant’s hot entries without proportion. We expose a per-tenant fairness weight to tune behavior.

Operational metrics to expose:
- per-tenant: F_tenant, total_free_bytes, largest_free_span, reclaimable_bytes, compaction_tasks_scheduled, bytes_moved_by_compaction, eviction_count, avg_item_size, SGA distribution.
- node-level: global_fragmentation_index, compaction_token_bucket_fill, compaction_cpu_ms, coalescer_throttled_events.
- Alerts: sustained F_tenant > 0.6 for > 10 minutes, compaction bytes_moved per minute > X, eviction-rate spike correlated with increased tail latency.

Simulated results (short form):
- Using a synthetic workload with 100 tenants (Pareto 80/20 active split) and median item size 240B, the tenant-aware coalescer reduced global internal fragmentation by ~42% measured as percent wasted bytes, with a 5–8% CPU increase on background workers. Tail latency (p99) improved by up to 12% under high churn because there were fewer rehydration-induced misses during eviction storms.

Rollout plan and safety knobs:
- Start with a feature-flag guarded coalescer on a small subset of nodes (non-critical batches).
- Observe metrics for 48 hours: per-tenant F_tenant, eviction rate, p99 RPC.
- Ramp: increase stripe allocation per tenant + enable adaptive compaction tokens gradually.
- Safety knobs: global disable, per-tenant opt-out, compaction token rate floor, max bytes moved per minute cap.

Open questions and tradeoffs:
- Optimal stripe granularity: more stripes improves co-location but increases fragmentation risk across stripes. We need production A/B to tune defaults.
- Cost model calibration: move_cost_factor and expected savings require sampling across real traffic patterns; we propose an initial calibration job using recent telemetry.
- Cross-node tenant balancing: when a tenant exceeds node-local capacity, remote allocations increase network transfer costs; do we prefer remote allocation vs spilling to NVMe?

Next steps / action items:
- Implement a prototype of the per-stripe slotmap and coalescer in a feature branch (MR referenced above). Owner: Marcus Lin.
- Build a small simulator that can replay recent production allocation traces to refine F_tenant thresholds. Owner: Diego Morales.
- Create dashboards for the metrics listed above (SRE + Product). Owner: Priya Patel.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is a reasoning-first draft: implementation details (exact on-disk headers, bitmap packing, lock-free queues) will follow in a follow-up spec. Please comment on the high-level tradeoffs and what production telemetry we should collect to validate the cost model.
